references.text: The parallel passage in Matthew where the crowd follows Jesus to a desolate place, and he heals their sick out of compassion.
The parallel passage in Mark where the crowd follows Jesus, and he welcomes them and begins to teach them because they were like sheep without a shepherd.
The parallel passage in John where a large crowd followed Jesus because they saw the signs he performed on the sick.
Jesus says that he must preach the gospel of the kingdom of God also to the other cities, for that is why he was sent – the same preaching about the kingdom of God as in Luke 9:11.
Jesus went through towns and villages, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God, which aligns with his ministry in Luke 9:11.

Jesus traveled throughout Galilee, teaching in the synagogues, proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease among the people – the combination of preaching about the kingdom of God and healing, as seen in Luke 9:11.
Jesus went around preaching the gospel of the kingdom and healing every disease, and he had compassion on the crowd – a similar theme to Luke 9:11.
Large crowds gathered to hear Jesus and be healed of their diseases, the same pattern of preaching and healing as in Luke 9:11.
A large crowd came to hear Jesus and be healed of their diseases – the combination of teaching and healing that also characterizes Luke 9:11.
Paul preached the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ, continuing Jesus' own ministry of speaking about the kingdom of God as in Luke 9:11.
